name: Speed Garage
summary: US garage house at UK rave pressure: a heavy four-to-the-floor kick (occasionally doubled or skipped into a 2-step lurch), snare/clap slamming 2 and 4 with skippy low-velocity snare bounces, and shuffling syncopated 16th hats where all the swing lives. Open hats sit on every 8th-note offbeat and everything leaves room for the warped jungle-derived sub-bass.

sounds.kick: Deep, housey 909-style kick with a short tail and light drive; punchy rather than subby so the Reese/sub bass carries the low end.
sounds.snare: Big 909 snare or clap on the backbeat plus a second skippy snare (lower, shorter) for the bounces; 12-bit SP-1200 crunch is period-correct.
sounds.hats: 909 open hat on the offbeats (often bit-reduced), short closed 16ths with a strong e-and-a accent contour, swung 60–65%.
sounds.percussion: Shaker under the hats, tambourine offbeats and congas for the US-house lane, high-passed breakbeat loops for grit.
sounds.cymbals: Crash on drop entrances and section markers; a bright ride for peak-time variations.

machines: E-mu SP-1200 — the drum sampler behind Double 99 'RipGroove' (owned)
Roland TR-909 — kick, snare, clap and open hat foundation (owned)
Roland TR-808 — clap layer and deeper kick layer (owned)
Akai S900 / MPC60 — 12-bit sampling and swing for the '97 sound (owned)
Korg M1 drums — organ-tune era kit (owned)
Jungle/breakbeat libraries — high-passed break loops as texture (owned)
Vinyl-texture and noise samples for glue (get elsewhere)
references: Sneaker Pimps — Spin Spin Sugar (Armand Van Helden Dark Garage Mix) (1997)
